/**
 * @brief Barrier synchronization structure for multi-core coordination.
 *
 * This structure is used to implement a barrier where multiple cores wait
 * until all participating cores have reached a certain point before continuing.
 */
typedef struct {
    volatile uint32_t flag;     /* indicate all cores have reached the barrier */
    volatile uint32_t bitmap;   /* record reach core info*/
 } barrier_t;

/**  
 * @brief Atomically compares and swaps a value in memory.  
 * @details This function implements an atomic Compare and Swap (CAS) operation  
 * that checks whether the value at a specified memory address matches  
 * the expected old value. If it does, it replaces it with a new value.  
 * This is typically used in multi-threaded environments to manage  
 * access to shared data safely, helping to prevent race conditions.   
 * @param addr      Pointer to the memory address where the value is  
 *                  stored. This address must be `volatile` to prevent  
 *                  compiler optimizations that could lead to incorrect  
 *                  behavior in a multi-threaded context.  
 * @param preval   The expected old value that is to be compared against  
 *                  the current value at the memory location pointed to by   
 *                  `addr`.  
 * @param value   The new value to write to the memory location if the  
 *                  comparison is successful (i.e., if the current value  
 *                  equals `preval`).    
 * @return The original value that was at the memory location before the  
 *         operation. This can be used to determine whether the swap  
 *         was successful; if it equals `preval`, then the operation succeeded.  
 *   
 * The function uses a loop with Load Reserved (lr) and Store Conditional (sc)  
 * instructions that are designed to be atomic.  
 * This mechanism is crucial for implementing lock-free data structures  
 * and algorithms.  
 */
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE uint32_t __CAS_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, uint32_t preval, uint32_t value)
{
    uint32_t result;
    uint32_t rc;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                                 \
            "0:     lr.w %0, %2      \n"            \
            "       bne  %0, %z3, 1f \n"            \
            "       sc.w %1, %z4, %2 \n"            \
            "       bnez %1, 0b      \n"            \
            "1:\n"                                  \
            : "=&r"(result), "=&r"(rc), "+A"(*addr) \
            : "r"(preval), "r"(value)               \
            : "memory");
    return result;
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically swaps a value in memory and returns the old value.  
 * @details This function implements an atomic swap operation using the AMOSWAP (Atomic Memory Swap) 
 * instruction. It takes a value and replaces the value at the specified memory address with  
 * the new value, while returning the old value that was at that address. 
 * This operation is typically used in multi-threaded environments to ensure that 
 * updates to shared resources are performed safely without race conditions.  
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory address where the value  
 *               will be swapped. This address must be `volatile`  
 *               to prevent compiler optimizations that may lead  
 *               to incorrect behavior in a concurrent context.  
 * @param value  The new value to be stored at the memory location  
 *               pointed to by `addr`. This is the value that will  
 *               replace the old value.  
 * @return The old value that was at the memory location before  
 *         the swap operation. This allows the caller to see what  
 *         value was replaced.   
 */ 
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE uint32_t __AMOSWAP_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, uint32_t value)
{
    uint32_t result;
    __ASM_VOLATILE(                     \
            "amoswap.w %0, %2, %1"      \
            :"=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)  \
            : "r"(value)                \
            : "memory");
    return result;
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically adds a value to a memory location and returns the new value.  
 * @details This function implements an atomic add operation using  
 * the AMOADD (Atomic Memory Add) instruction. It adds a specified   
 * value to the integer located at the provided memory address   
 * atomically, and it returns the new value stored at that address.   
 * This operation ensures that updates to shared resources are   
 * performed safely in a multi-threaded environment, preventing   
 * race conditions. 
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory address where the value  
 *               will be added. This address must be `volatile`  
 *               to prevent compiler optimizations that may lead  
 *               to incorrect behavior in a concurrent context.  
 * @param value  The value to be added to the integer at the memory   
 *               location pointed to by `addr`.  
 *  
 * @return The new value at the memory location after the addition   
 *         has been performed. This allows the caller to see the   
 *         value after the atomic addition.  
 * 
 * This mechanism is crucial for implementing lock-free data   
 * structures and algorithms, as it allows safe access and  
 * modification of shared data in a concurrent programming  
 * environment.  
 */
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE int32_t __AMOADD_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, int32_t value)
{
    int32_t result;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                         \
            "amoadd.w %0, %2, %1"           \
            :"=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)      \
            : "r"(value)                    \
            : "memory");
    return *addr;
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically performs a bitwise AND on a memory location and returns the new value.  
 * @details This function implements an atomic bitwise AND operation using the  
 * AMOAND (Atomic Memory AND) instruction. It performs a bitwise AND   
 * between a specified value and the integer located at the provided   
 * memory address atomically, returning the new value stored at that   
 * memory location. 
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory address where the bitwise AND   
 *               operation will be performed. This address must be   
 *               `volatile` to prevent compiler optimizations that may   
 *               lead to incorrect behavior in a concurrent context.  
 * @param value  The value to be ANDed with the integer at the memory   
 *               location pointed to by `addr`.  
 * @return The new value at the memory location after the AND operation   
 *         has been performed. 
 *  
 * This mechanism is crucial for implementing lock-free data   
 * structures and algorithms, as it allows safe access and   
 * modification of shared data in a concurrent programming   
 * environment.  
 */
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE int32_t __AMOAND_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, int32_t value)
{
    int32_t result;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                         \
            "amoand.w %0, %2, %1"           \
            :"=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)      \
            : "r"(value)                    \
            : "memory");
    return *addr;
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically performs a bitwise OR on a memory location and returns the new value.  
 * @details This function implements an atomic bitwise OR operation using the  
 * AMOOR (Atomic Memory OR) instruction. It performs a bitwise OR   
 * between a specified value and the integer located at the provided   
 * memory address atomically, returning the new value stored at that   
 * memory location.  
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory address where the bitwise OR   
 *               operation will be performed. This address must be   
 *               `volatile` to prevent compiler optimizations that may   
 *               lead to incorrect behavior in a concurrent context.  
 * @param value  The value to be ORed with the integer at the memory   
 *               location pointed to by `addr`.  
 * @return The new value at the memory location after the OR operation   
 *         has been performed. This allows the caller to see the value   
 *         after the atomic operation.  
 *  
 * This mechanism is crucial for implementing lock-free data   
 * structures and algorithms, as it allows safe access and   
 * modification of shared data in a concurrent programming   
 * environment.  
 */
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE int32_t __AMOOR_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, int32_t value)
{
    int32_t result;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                         \
            "amoor.w %0, %2, %1"            \
            :"=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)      \
            : "r"(value)                    \
            : "memory");
    return *addr;
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically performs a bitwise XOR on a memory location and returns the new value.  
 * @details This function implements an atomic bitwise XOR operation using the  
 * AMOXOR (Atomic Memory XOR) instruction. It performs a bitwise XOR   
 * between a specified value and the integer located at the provided   
 * memory address atomically. It returns the new value stored at that   
 * memory location.
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory address where the bitwise XOR   
 *               operation will be performed. This address must be   
 *               `volatile` to prevent compiler optimizations that may   
 *               lead to incorrect behavior in a concurrent context.  
 * @param value  The value to be XORed with the integer at the memory   
 *               location pointed to by `addr`.  
 * @return The new value at the memory location after the XOR operation   
 *         has been performed. This allows the caller to see the value   
 *         after the atomic operation.  
 *  
 * This mechanism is crucial for implementing lock-free data   
 * structures and algorithms, as it allows safe access and   
 * modification of shared data in a concurrent programming   
 * environment.  
 */
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE int32_t __AMOXOR_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, int32_t value)
{
    int32_t result;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                     \
            "amoxor.w %0, %2, %1"       \
            :"=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)  \
            : "r"(value)                \
            : "memory");
    return *addr;
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically computes the maximum of the value at a memory location and the specified value.  
 * @details This function implements an atomic maximum operation for unsigned integers   
 * using the AMOMAXU (Atomic Memory Maximum Unsigned) instruction. It compares   
 * the current unsigned integer value at the provided memory address with a   
 * specified value, and stores the maximum of the two back to the memory location   
 * atomically.
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory address where the maximum operation   
 *               will be performed. This address must be `volatile` to   
 *               prevent compiler optimizations that may lead to incorrect   
 *               behavior in a concurrent context.  
 * @param value  The unsigned integer value to be compared against the value  
 *               at the memory location referenced by `addr`.  
 * @return The value at the memory location after the maximum operation   
 *         has been performed.
 *  
 * This mechanism is crucial for implementing lock-free data structures and   
 * algorithms, as it allows safe access and modification of shared data in   
 * a concurrent programming environment.  
 */
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE uint32_t __AMOMAXU_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, uint32_t value)
{
    uint32_t result;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                          \
            "amomaxu.w %0, %2, %1"           \
            :"=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)       \
            : "r"(value)                     \
            : "memory");
    return *addr;
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically compute the maximum of a memory value and a specified value.  
 * @details This function performs an atomic comparison between the signed integer   
 * value at the specified memory location (pointed by `addr`) and the   
 * provided `value`. It updates the memory location with the maximum   
 * of the two values atomically.
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory location (volatile int32_t) where   
 *               the maximum operation will be performed.
 * @param value  The signed integer value to be compared with the current   
 *               value at the memory location pointed to by `addr`.  
 * @return The value stored at the memory location after the maximum   
 *         operation has been performed. 
 *  
 * This function is particularly useful in multi-threaded programming   
 * environments where multiple threads may attempt to update the same   
 * memory location simultaneously. By using atomic operations, it ensures   
 * that the updates are safe and prevents race conditions.  
 */  
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE int32_t __AMOMAX_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, int32_t value)  
{  
    int32_t result;  

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                     \
        "amomax.w %0, %2, %1"           \
        :"=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)      \
        : "r"(value)                    \
        : "memory");  

    return *addr; 
}

/**  
 * @brief  Atomically compute the minimum of a memory value and a specified value.  
 * @details This function performs an atomic comparison between the unsigned integer   
 * value at the specified memory location (pointed by `addr`) and the   
 * provided `value`. It updates the memory location with the minimum   
 * of the two values atomically.
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory location (volatile uint32_t) where   
 *               the minimum operation will be performed. 
 * @param value  The unsigned integer value to be compared with the current   
 *               value at the memory location pointed to by `addr`.  
 * @return The value stored at the memory location after the minimum   
 *         operation has been performed. 
 * 
 * This function is particularly useful in multi-threaded programming   
 * environments where multiple threads may attempt to update the same   
 * memory location simultaneously. By utilizing atomic operations, it   
 * ensures that the updates are safe and prevents race conditions.  
 */ 
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE uint32_t __AMOMINU_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, uint32_t value)
{
    uint32_t result;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                           \
            "amominu.w %0, %2, %1"            \
            : "=r"(result), "+A"(*addr)       \
            : "r"(value)                      \

    return *addr;
}

/**  
 * @brief Atomically compute the minimum of a memory value and a specified value.  
 * @details This function performs an atomic comparison between the signed integer   
 * value at the specified memory location (pointed by `addr`) and the   
 * provided `value`. It updates the memory location with the minimum   
 * of the two values atomically. 
 *  
 * @param addr   Pointer to the memory location (volatile int32_t) where   
 *               the minimum operation will be performed. T
 * @param value  The signed integer value to be compared with the current   
 *               value at the memory location pointed to by `addr`.  
 * @return The value stored at the memory location after the minimum   
 *         operation has been performed. 
 * 
 * This function is particularly useful in multi-threaded programming   
 * environments where multiple threads may attempt to update the same   
 * memory location simultaneously. By utilizing atomic operations, it   
 * ensures that the updates are safe and prevents race conditions.  
 */
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE int32_t __AMOMIN_W(volatile uint32_t *addr, int32_t value)
{
    int32_t result;

    __ASM_VOLATILE(                           \

            : "memory");
    return *addr;
}

/**
 * @brief Initialize a barrier synchronization structure.
 * This function initializes the barrier's internal state with default values:
 * - Sets the flag to a recognizable magic number (0x5A5A5A5A)
 * - Clears the core arrival bitmap to 0
 * @param barrier Pointer to the barrier structure to initialize.
 * 
 * @note The magic number (0x5A5A5A5A) helps detect uninitialized barriers
 *       and provides a known starting state for the flag.
 */
 __STATIC_FORCEINLINE void barrier_init(barrier_t *barrier)
 {
     if (barrier != NULL)
     {
         barrier->flag = 0x5a5a5a5a;
         barrier->bitmap = 0;
     }
 }
 
/**
 * @brief Wait at a barrier until all specified cores arrive.
 * This function implements a multi-core barrier synchronization mechanism.
 * Each core sets its bit in the barrier's bitmap and waits until all specified
 * cores have arrived (bitmap matches corebitmap), at which point the barrier flag
 * is toggled to release all waiting cores
 * @param barrier Pointer to the barrier structure containing synchronization state.
 * @param corebitmap Bitmask representing which cores must arrive at the barrier
 *                  (each bit represents a core, e.g., 0b1111 for 4 cores).
 * @warning The barrier structure must be properly initialized before use.
 *          The corebitmap must match the actual number of participating cores.
 */
 __STATIC_FORCEINLINE void barrier_wait(barrier_t *barrier, uint32_t corebitmap)
{
    uint32_t coreid = __get_hart_id(); // Get the current core ID
    uint32_t flag = barrier->flag;

    /* set the bitmap, barrier->bitmap |= bitmap*/
    __AMOOR_W(&barrier->bitmap, 1 << coreid);

    /* all cores have reached the barrier, set the flag */
    if (barrier->bitmap == corebitmap)
    {
        barrier->flag = ~flag;
        barrier->bitmap = 0;
    }

    /* wait until all cores reach the barrier */
    while (barrier->flag == flag)
    {
        /* spin-wait */
    }
}
#endif /*__CORE_ATOMIC_H__*/

/****************************** Fence Operations **********************************/
#define __FENCE(p, s) __ASM_VOLATILE("fence " STR(p) "," STR(s) : : : "memory")

/** @brief Read & Write Memory barrier */
#define __RWMB()                 __FENCE(iorw, iorw)

/** @brief Read Memory barrier */
#define __RMB()                  __FENCE(ir, ir)

/** @brief Write Memory barrier */
#define __WMB()                  __FENCE(ow, ow)

/** @brief Data Synchronization Barrier, compatiable with ARM */

/**  
 * @brief Swap the value of a Control and Status Register (CSR) with a given value.  
 * This macro performs a read-modify-write operation on a specified RISC-V  
 * Control and Status Register (CSR). It reads the current value of the CSR,  
 * replaces it with the specified value, and returns the original value of the CSR.  
 * @param csr The CSR register to be modified. Should be specified as a valid CSR identifier.  
 * @param val The new value to write into the CSR. This value will replace the current CSR value.  
 * @return The previous value of the CSR before the new value was written.   
 * @note   
 * This macro uses inline assembly to perform the operation atomically. It is important to ensure  
 * that the CSR being accessed is appropriate for the operation being performed.   
 * The macro elides the assembly details from the user and provides a convenient interface for   
 * interacting with CSRs.    
 */ 
#define __CSR_SWAP(csr, val)                                    \
    ({                                                          \
        wm_csr_t __tmp = (wm_csr_t)(val);                       \
        __ASM_VOLATILE("csrrw %0, " STR(csr) ", %1"             \
                     : "=r"(__tmp)                              \
                     : "rK"(__tmp)                              \
                     : "memory");                               \
        __tmp;                                                  \
    })

/**  
 * @brief Read a value from a Control and Status Register (CSR).  
 * This macro reads the current value of a specified RISC-V Control   
 * and Status Register (CSR) and returns it.  
 * @param csr The CSR register to be read. Should be specified as a valid CSR identifier.  
 * @return The current value of the specified CSR.   
 * @note   
 * This macro uses inline assembly to perform the read operation. It   
 * ensures that the read value is retrieved atomically. The result   
 * can be used directly in further computations or logic. 
 */
#define __CSR_READ(csr)                                         \
    ({                                                          \
        wm_csr_t __tmp;                                         \
        __ASM_VOLATILE("csrr %0, " STR(csr)                     \
                     : "=r"(__tmp)                              \
                     :                                          \
                     : "memory");                               \
        __tmp;                                                  \
    })

/**  
 * @brief Write a value to a Control and Status Register (CSR).  
 * This macro writes a specified value to a designated RISC-V   
 * Control and Status Register (CSR).   
 * @param csr The CSR register to be written to. Should be specified as a valid CSR identifier.  
 * @param val The value to write into the specified CSR.  
 * @note   
 * This macro uses inline assembly to perform the write operation.   
 * The operation is performed atomically to ensure the integrity of the register.   
 * It does not return any value, as it simply writes to the CSR.    
 */ 
#define __CSR_WRITE(csr, val)                                   \
    ({                                                          \
        wm_csr_t __tmp = (wm_csr_t)(val);                       \
        __ASM_VOLATILE("csrw " STR(csr) ", %0"                  \
                     :                                          \
                     : "rK"(__tmp)                              \
                     : "memory");                               \
    })

/**  
 * @brief Read the value from a Control and Status Register (CSR) and set specific bits.   
 * This macro reads the current value of a specified RISC-V Control   
 * and Status Register (CSR), sets specific bits as defined by the   
 * provided value, and returns the original value of the CSR.  
 * @param csr The CSR register to be modified. Should be specified as a valid CSR identifier.  
 * @param val The value containing the bits to be set in the CSR. Only the bits set in this value will be affected.  
 * @return The previous value of the CSR before the bits were set.  
 * @note   
 * This macro utilizes inline assembly to perform the read-modify-write   
 * operation atomically. The `csrrs` instruction reads the CSR value,   
 * sets the bits specified by the provided value, and returns the old CSR value.  
 * This is useful when you want to modify specific bits of a CSR without   
 * affecting other bits.   
 */ 
#define __CSR_READ_SET(csr, val)                                \
    ({                                                          \
        wm_csr_t __tmp = (wm_csr_t)(val);                       \
        __ASM_VOLATILE("csrrs %0, " STR(csr) ", %1"             \
                     : "=r"(__tmp)                              \
                     : "rK"(__tmp)                              \
                     : "memory");                               \
        __tmp;                                                  \
    })

/**  
 * @brief Set specific bits in a Control and Status Register (CSR).  
 * This macro sets specific bits in a designated RISC-V Control   
 * and Status Register (CSR) based on the provided value.   
 * Only the bits that are set in the value will be modified, while

 * @param csr The CSR register to be modified. Should be specified as a valid CSR identifier.

        wm_csr_t __tmp = (wm_csr_t)(val);                       \

/**  
 * @brief Switches execution context from machine mode to another privilege mode.  
 *   
 * This function allows changing the execution mode from machine mode to   
 * either supervisor or user mode. It sets up the stack pointer and the   
 * entry point for the new context.  
 *  
 * @param mode   The privilege mode to switch to. It should be specified   
 *               using the appropriate mode constants (e.g., user mode or   
 *               supervisor mode).  
 * @param stack  The predefined stack address for the new context. The   
 *               size of the stack must be sufficient for the expected   
 *               execution.  
 * @param entry  A function pointer to the function to execute in the new   
 *               context.    
 */  
__STATIC_FORCEINLINE void __switch_mode_from_machine(PRIVILEGE_TYPE mode, uintptr_t stack, void(*entry)(void))
{
    unsigned long val = 0;

    /* Set MPP to the requested privilege mode */
    val = __CSR_READ(CSR_MSTATUS);
    val = INSERT_FIELD(val, MSTATUS_MPP, mode);

    /* Set previous MIE disabled */
    val = INSERT_FIELD(val, MSTATUS_MPIE, 0);

    __CSR_WRITE(CSR_MSTATUS, val);

    /* Set the entry point in MEPC */
    __CSR_WRITE(CSR_MEPC, (unsigned long)entry);

    /* Set the register file */
    __ASM_VOLATILE("mv sp, %0" ::"r"(stack));

    __ASM_VOLATILE("mret");
}

#include "rv_encoding.h"
#include "rv_common.h"

  .section ".text.init"
  .globl _start
  .type _start, @function
_start:
  li  x1, 0
  li  x2, 0
  li  x3, 0
  li  x4, 0
  li  x5, 0
  li  x6, 0
  li  x7, 0
  li  x8, 0
  li  x9, 0
  li  x10,0
  li  x11,0
  li  x12,0
  li  x13,0
  li  x14,0
  li  x15,0
#ifdef __riscv_isa_i    
  li  x16,0
  li  x17,0
  li  x18,0
  li  x19,0
  li  x20,0
  li  x21,0
  li  x22,0
  li  x23,0
  li  x24,0
  li  x25,0
  li  x26,0
  li  x27,0
  li  x28,0
  li  x29,0
  li  x30,0
  li  x31,0
#endif

  # enable FPU
#ifdef __riscv_flen
  li t0, MSTATUS_FS
  csrs mstatus, t0
#endif

#ifdef __riscv_vector
    /* Enable Vector, and set state to initial */
    li t0, MSTATUS_VS
    csrc mstatus, t0
    li t0, MSTATUS_VS_INITIAL
    csrs mstatus, t0
#endif

  # initialize trap vector,only for startup phase 
  la t0, boot_exception_entry
  csrw mtvec, t0

  # initialize global pointer
.option push
.option norelax
  la gp, __global_pointer$
.option pop

#ifdef __riscv_jvt
  # Initialize table jump base
  la a0, __jvt_base$
  csrw jvt, a0
#endif

  la      sp, __STACK_END

# load text section from storage to destination
1:
  la    a0, __TXET_LOAD_START
  la    a1, __TEXT_DESTINATION_START
  la    a2, __TEXT_DESTINATION_END
  beq   a0, a1, 1f
  j     3f
2:  
  lw    a3, 0(a0)
  sw    a3, 0(a1)
  add   a0, a0, 4
  add   a1, a1, 4
3:  
  bne   a1, a2, 2b

# load data section from storage to destination
1:
  la    a0, __DATA_LOAD_START
  la    a1, __DATA_DESTINATION_START
  la    a2, __DATA_DESTINATION_END
  beq   a0, a1, 1f
  j     3f
2:  
  lw    a3, 0(a0)
  sw    a3, 0(a1)
  add   a0, a0, 4
  add   a1, a1, 4
3:  
  bne   a1, a2, 2b  
 
# clear bss
1:
  la a0, __BSS_START
  la a1, __BSS_END
  bgeu a0, a1, 1f
2:
  sw zero, (a0)
  addi a0, a0, 4
  bltu a0, a1, 2b

1: 
#ifdef __SEMIHOSTING
  call init_semihosting
#endif
  call System_PreInit

#ifdef rtos_rtthread
  // Call entry function of RT-Thread
  call entry
#else
  call main
#endif

  call   System_PostFini
  j nmi_trap_entry #never run here,just avoid optimization

# exception entry before main
.align 6
.global boot_exception_entry
boot_exception_entry:
  j boot_exception_entry
.size _start, .-_start

#if defined(__CLIC_PRESENT) && (__CLIC_PRESENT == 1)
.section ".text.trap"
.align 6
.weak trap_entry
.type trap_entry, @function
trap_entry:
#--------------interrupt disable--------------
  addi sp, sp, -SW_CONTEXT_REG_NUM*REGBYTES
  SAVE_CONTEXT
  csrr a0, mcause
  mv a1, sp
  blez a0, int_proc
  call System_TrapHandler
int_proc:  
  
  csrrsi a0, mnxti, MSTATUS_MIE
#--------------interrupt enable---------------
  beqz a0, exit
service_loop:
  LREG a1, (a0)
  csrrsi zero, mstatus, MSTATUS_MIE
  jalr a1
  csrrsi a0, mnxti, MSTATUS_MIE
  bnez a0, service_loop

#------------no interrupt is pending----------
exit:
  csrrci zero, mstatus, MSTATUS_MIE 
#---------------interrupt disable---------------
  RESTORE_CONTEXT
  csrrci a0, mnxti, MSTATUS_MIE

  bnez a0, service_loop
  lw a0, A0_OFFSET(sp)
  addi sp, sp, SW_CONTEXT_REG_NUM*REGBYTES
  mret
.size trap_entry, .-trap_entry
#else
.section ".text.trap"
  /* In CLINT mode, the trap entry must be 4 bytes aligned */
  .align 2
  .weak trap_entry
  .type trap_entry, @function
trap_entry:
  addi sp, sp, -SW_CONTEXT_REG_NUM*REGBYTES
  SAVE_CONTEXT
  csrr a0, mcause
  mv a1, sp
  call System_TrapHandler
  RESTORE_CONTEXT
  addi sp, sp, SW_CONTEXT_REG_NUM*REGBYTES
  mret
.size trap_entry, .-trap_entry
#endif

.section ".text.trap.nmi"
.balign 512
.type nmi_trap_entry, @function
.weak nmi_trap_entry
nmi_trap_entry:
  addi sp, sp, -SW_CONTEXT_REG_NUM*REGBYTES
  SAVE_CONTEXT

#if defined(__RNMI_PRESENT) && (__RNMI_PRESENT == 1)
  csrr a0, mncause
#else
  csrr a0, mcause  
#endif  
  mv a1, sp
  call System_NMIHandler
  
  RESTORE_CONTEXT
  addi sp, sp, SW_CONTEXT_REG_NUM*REGBYTES

#if defined(__RNMI_PRESENT) && (__RNMI_PRESENT == 1)
  mnret
#else
  mret
#endif  
.size nmi_trap_entry, .-nmi_trap_entry
